scorecards.inningsCommentary: New Zealand commenced their first innings at Seddon Park, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 84 from JA Raval, complemented by a commanding 89-run stand between JA Raval and Kane Williamson that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.56 RPO. West Indies's bowling response was spearheaded by ST Gabriel (4/111), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Concluding at 373/10 (102.2 ov), New Zealand posted a competitive total, ensuring a closely matched contest.

Reaching 221/10 (66.5 ov), West Indies's innings completed the first-innings exchange (152 Runs (New Zealand)), shaping the strategic contours for the second half of the Test.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: West Indies embarked on a high-stakes fourth-innings chase of 444 Runs, confronting a deteriorating pitch and aggressive field settings. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 64 from RL Chase, complemented by a commanding 78-run stand between RA Reifer and RL Chase that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.17 RPO. New Zealand's bowling response was spearheaded by Neil Wagner (4/41), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Dismissed for 203/10 (63.5 ov), West Indies succumbed to fourth-innings pressure as New Zealand's bowlers closed out the victory.

West Indies responded with 221 as both teams traded momentum in high-stakes middle sessions. A ruthless second-innings declaration at 291/8d by New Zealand established a massive 444 Runs target. Neil Wagner spearheaded New Zealand's attack to bowl out West Indies for 203 and seal victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Seddon Park commenced with high tactical intensity as New Zealand posted 373/10 (102.2 ov) in their opening innings. In response, West Indies countered with 221/10 (66.5 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: LRPL Taylor 107 (199b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Trent Boult delivered a masterclass for New Zealand (37 Runs & 6 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (New Zealand 55%) and allowing New Zealand to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, West Indies faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. New Zealand's bowling unit, bolstered by Tim Southee (53 Runs & 4 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing New Zealand won by 240 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: New Zealand's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While West Indies produced fighting phases, New Zealand won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
